title: Life in the Simulation Machine
coreMove: Make every abstraction prove where it touches reality and who pays when the model is wrong.
sourcePressure: Model-driven understanding becomes suspect when the person designing the model does not absorb the cost of its errors.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Attacking models as such, instead of attacking no-consequence models that outrun field correction.

sourceAnchors.name: Life in the Simulation Machine
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen chapter title and sidecar support the contrast between simulated understanding and reality-tested judgment, with no named anecdote frozen.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Use the simulation machine as a boundary image: the problem is not thinking in models, but never feeling the model break.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: urban traffic model tested against an icy intersection
exampleSpecs.audience: planner whose simulation says a turn lane is safe
exampleSpecs.stakes: drivers will pay for a model that never stood in sleet
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily stands at the crosswalk during freezing rain and changes the model assumption after watching trucks swing wide.

exampleSpecs.domain: warehouse robot rollout based on clean demo-floor paths
exampleSpecs.audience: operations lead discovering field clutter absent from simulation
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed edge cases could injure pickers and halt shipments
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas pauses rollout until the robot navigates the real aisle with loose wrap and dented pallets.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: plastic wrap caught under a wheel

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital staffing forecast built without night-shift observation
exampleSpecs.audience: scheduler relying on averages without carrying error cost
exampleSpecs.stakes: nurses absorb the mismatch when patient surges hit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ingrid asks the model owner to work one midnight triage shift before approving the staffing cut.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: blue light over a triage desk

exampleSpecs.domain: fisheries quota spreadsheet ignoring dockside discard behavior
exampleSpecs.audience: policy analyst checking model output against boats returning
exampleSpecs.stakes: families and stock health pay if clean assumptions miss dirty practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sam changes the quota memo after counting unsellable bycatch on the dock.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: wet scales on a dock clipboard

exampleSpecs.domain: insurance wildfire map drawn by analysts far from the valley
exampleSpecs.audience: underwriter deciding whether remote risk bands match actual brush conditions
exampleSpecs.stakes: homeowners may buy false security priced by distant abstraction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Catarina walks the evacuation road and adds a field exception the model would not see.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: charred fence posts along a gravel road

exampleSpecs.domain: court scheduling algorithm that ignores childcare constraints
exampleSpecs.audience: administrator testing software against hallway reality
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed appearances become warrants for people the model abstracts away
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Akira traces three missed hearings to daycare closing time and rewrites the scheduling rule.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a courthouse hallway clock above folded strollers
